title: Total lifting squares reduce to a fibre by adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be an ordinary category [def-nagata-category] and let $s\mapsto M_s$ be a strict contravariant diagram of categories: a map $r:s\to t$ gives $r^*:M_t\to M_s$, with $(qr)^*=r^*q^*$ and $1^*=1$. Assume each $r^*$ has a left adjoint $r_!$, with a natural Hom bijection $\Phi_r:\operatorname{Hom}(r_!P,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,r^*Q)$. Define its total category to have objects $(s,P)$, arrows $(r,z):(s,P)\to(t,Q)$ with $z:P\to r^*Q$, and composition $(q,z')(r,z)=(qr,r^*z'\circ z)$. Let a commuting square have left arrow $(f,v):(s,A)\to(t,B)$, right arrow $(g,w):(u,X)\to(v_0,Y)$, top arrow $(a,\alpha)$ and bottom arrow $(b,\beta)$. Thus $ga=bf$ and $a^*w\circ\alpha=f^*\beta\circ v$. Fix $h:t\to u$ with $hf=a$ and $gh=b$. Put $u_f=\Phi_f^{-1}(v)$, $\widetilde\alpha=\Phi_h^{-1}(\Phi_f^{-1}(\alpha)):h_!f_!A\to X$, and $\widetilde\beta=\Phi_h^{-1}(\beta):h_!B\to g^*Y$, using $a^*=f^*h^*$ and $b^*=h^*g^*$. Then
$$w\widetilde\alpha=\widetilde\beta\circ h_!u_f.$$
Moreover $d\mapsto\Phi_h^{-1}(d)$ is a bijection between total diagonals over $h$, namely $d:B\to h^*X$ with $f^*d\circ v=\alpha$ and $h^*w\circ d=\beta$, and fibre diagonals $\delta:h_!B\to X$ with $\delta\circ h_!u_f=\widetilde\alpha$ and $w\delta=\widetilde\beta$. Its inverse is $\delta\mapsto\Phi_h(\delta)$. No model structure, injectivity of base maps or equivalence of the adjoints is assumed.

source.place: Haugseng, Proposition 4.25, proof of the lifting assertion in Section 4.3. This isolates the ordinary total-to-fibre square comparison used there; the statement gives its precise adjunction equations. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag supplies this particular comparison.
